pages.name: Two moves, one matrix
pages.text: In `AB` the right-hand card acts first. B turns the flag a quarter, and a ghost stays where it lands. Then A leans it. Each move keeps the grid a grid, with the origin fixed. So one matrix makes the whole run, `AB = [1 −1; 1 0]`.

pages.name: Where i ends
pages.task: Where does i end up after B, then A?
pages.why: B turns i a quarter, from `(1, 0)` to `(0, 1)`. The shear A then pushes that point one square across, to `(1, 1)`. So column 1 of `AB` is `(1, 1)`.

pages.name: Where j ends
pages.text: B turns j to `(−1, 0)`. The shear leaves every point on the across axis where it is, so j stays there. The run is one move, so the columns of `AB` are where i and j end up, `(1, 1)` and `(−1, 0)`.

pages.name: Swap the cards
pages.task: The cards are swapped, so the shear acts first. Which matrix is `BA`?
pages.why: The shear acts first. It leaves i at `(1, 0)` and sends j to `(1, 1)`. The turn then sends those to `(0, 1)` and `(−1, 1)`. So `BA = [0 −1; 1 1]`.

pages.name: Both orders
pages.text: Here `AB` and `BA` run side by side. The same two moves in opposite orders usually leave the flag in different places. Do nothing is the [[identity matrix]] `[1 0; 0 1]`. pages.name: Which comes first?
pages.task: First comes the shear S, then the mirror `M = [−1 0; 0 1]`. Which product is that?
pages.why: In a product the right-hand card acts first. The shear comes first, so S goes on the right. That gives `MS`.

pages.name: Row times column
pages.text: Each entry of `AB` is a row of A times a column of B. Column 1 of B is where B sends i. A then works on that point, one row at a time. Row 1 of A meets column 1 of B pair by pair, so the top-left is `1 × 0 + 1 × 1 = 1`. So a row and a column must be the same length. The other three entries come the same way, giving `[1 −1; 1 0]`.
